agreement.meaning: Share of models agreeing on the direction of change taken by the majority (the paper's 'model agreement', 50-100%). Negative = the majority projects a decline, positive = an increase; |value| is the paper's agreement.

median.meaning: Ensemble MEDIAN of the same percentage changes (not shown in the paper). Unlike the mean it is not pulled by one model's extreme values, e.g. DBEM's several-hundred-% gains from near-zero baselines in the Southern Ocean at 50-60°S.

display.meaning: The ensemble median resampled to 0.25° for display: coastal ocean cells filled from the nearest model cell (up to 2°), land blanked (Natural Earth 1:50m).

global.note: Mean over the 16 model pairs of each pair's change in global total animal biomass, relative to 1990-1999, from the paper's time-series data (Fig. 3). Global numbers only: the source has no maps for the 2040s.

source.citation: Tittensor, D. P. et al. (2021) Next-generation ensemble projections reveal higher climate risks for marine ecosystems. Nature Climate Change 11, 973-981. doi:10.1038/s41558-021-01173-9
source.variable: tcb, total consumer biomass: total marine animal biomass without fishing; the animals represented vary among models but generally include major taxonomic groups or major fish taxa

ensemble.IPSL-CM6A-LR: 9: APECOSM, BOATS, DBPM, MACROECOLOGICAL, FEISTY, ZooMSS, EcoTroph, EcoOcean, DBEM
ensemble.GFDL-ESM4: 6: BOATS, MACROECOLOGICAL, ZooMSS, FEISTY, EcoTroph, DBEM
ensemble.excluded: GFDL-ESM4 x EcoOcean: in the archived map data its 2090s fields are the IPSL-CM6A-LR ones (a file-path slip in the paper's map script), so its change is not a valid GFDL projection

source.method: For each model pair, decadal-mean biomass in 2090-2099 divided by 1990-1999 on a 1° grid; the map is the unweighted mean of these percentage changes across model pairs (as the paper's model_stat), clipped to ±50%; agreement is the share of pairs on the majority side.
source.periods: Only 2090-2099 vs 1990-1999 exists as maps in this source; no mid-century maps.
